events.asset: MAPP2 (NCT04077437), the second Phase 3 trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD
events.title: MAPP2 Phase 3 trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD meets its primary endpoint
events.proposition: MAPP2 (NCT04077437), the second Phase 3 trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD, reports its prespecified primary endpoint met with statistical significance.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the sponsor's topline release, the ClinicalTrials.gov results posting or the peer-reviewed publication that first reports that MAPP2 (NCT04077437), the second Phase 3 trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD, met its prespecified primary endpoint (change in CAPS-5 total severity score versus placebo with therapy) with statistical significance as reported by the sponsor. FALSE on the date the sponsor first reports that the primary endpoint was not met, and FALSE at the deadline when no primary-endpoint result has been reported. Secondary endpoints, interim analyses and pooled analyses do not count. Resolution source: the ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT04077437 (results section), with the sponsor's topline press release or the first publication fixing the date.

resolution_source.name: ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT04077437 (results); sponsor topline press release or first publication as the secondary source

readings: 'the second phase three study looks good' reads as MAPP2 meeting its prespecified primary endpoint with statistical significance.

events.asset: psilocybin drug product (any sponsor, any indication): first Phase 3 trial start

events.proposition: A sponsor starts a Phase 3 clinical trial of a psilocybin drug product for any indication.
events.criterion: TRUE on the earlier of (a) the date of a sponsor press release that announces the first participant enrolled or dosed in a trial registered as Phase 3 on ClinicalTrials.gov or the EU Clinical Trials Register whose investigational product is psilocybin, for any indication, or (b) the actual study start date recorded for such a trial on ClinicalTrials.gov. events.asset: DEA February 2023 proposed rule on telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances
events.title: DEA February 2023 proposed telemedicine controlled-substance rule is revised, withdrawn or replaced
events.proposition: DEA revises, withdraws or replaces its February 2023 proposed rule on telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances rather than finalizing it as proposed.
events.criterion: TRUE on the Federal Register publication date of a DEA action on its February 2023 proposed rule on telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances without a prior in-person medical evaluation that departs from finalizing the proposal as written: a final rule whose operative requirements differ materially from the proposal (for example on the in-person evaluation requirement), a formal withdrawal of the proposal, or a new proposed rule that supersedes it. FALSE on the Federal Register publication date of a final rule that adopts the February 2023 proposal without material change, and FALSE at the deadline when the proposal has been neither revised, withdrawn nor replaced. events.asset: TMS (including accelerated protocols) as a first-line treatment for major depressive disorder
events.title: A depression practice guideline lists TMS as a first-line treatment
events.proposition: The American Psychiatric Association issues a practice guideline for major depressive disorder that lists TMS (including accelerated protocols) as a first-line treatment option.
events.criterion: TRUE on the publication date of an American Psychiatric Association practice guideline, or guideline update, for major depressive disorder that recommends TMS (any protocol, including accelerated protocols) or another non-ECT neuromodulation modality as a first-line treatment option, that is, as an initial treatment not conditioned on prior antidepressant failure. A draft for comment, a payer policy, or a recommendation limited to treatment-resistant depression is not adoption. Resolution source: the APA Practice Guidelines (psychiatryonline.org). FALSE at the deadline when no such APA guideline has been published.
readings: 'Neuromodulation (especially accelerated TMS)' resolves on TMS; another non-ECT neuromodulation modality listed as first-line for MDD also counts.
ECT does not count: its existing role in severe or psychotic depression is not the change the claim describes.

'First-line treatment for depression' means the guideline lists the modality as an initial treatment option for MDD without requiring prior antidepressant failure; a listing only for treatment-resistant depression does not count.

events.asset: DEA COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances
events.title: DEA extends the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for controlled-substance prescribing past the PHE end
events.proposition: DEA issues a rule or order that extends the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances beyond the end of the COVID-19 public health emergency.
events.criterion: TRUE on the Federal Register publication date (or the DEA announcement date, if earlier) of a temporary rule or order that extends the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances beyond the end of the COVID-19 public health emergency, so that the Ryan Haight Act in-person visit requirement does not return for telehealth patients at the PHE end. A proposed rule is not an extension. FALSE when the flexibilities expire at the PHE end with no such rule or order published, and FALSE at the deadline when no extension appears in the Federal Register. Resolution source: the Federal Register.
readings: 'The Ryan Haight Act returns', 'in-office visits return for everybody everywhere' and an 'instant' return to in-person providers are read as the in-person requirement applying again to all telehealth controlled-substance patients at the PHE end.
Any DEA rule or order that continues remote prescribing of controlled substances without an in-person visit past the PHE end counts as an extension.

events.asset: SAINT Neuromodulation (Magnus Medical): Medicare new technology add-on payment (NTAP)
